in_hebrew.name: דמילה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: דם (dam) - blood, life force; אלה (elah) - strong, powerful, noble; in Hebrew, the name Damiella signifies a powerful and noble individual, strong in spirit and life force, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of Jewish and Christian traditions. In biblical context, blood symbolizes life, sacrifice, and redemption, while elah conveys strength and nobility. The name Damiella embodies the spiritual qualities of resilience, courage, and compassion, reflecting the ideals of Christian values.

in_greek.name: Δαμιέλα
in_greek.long_meaning: αίμα (aíma) - blood, life force; ελάσσονα (elassona) - less, smaller; in Greek, the name Damiella represents a subtle yet powerful spirit, a gentle soul with a strong inner life force, reflecting the cultural significance of blood as a symbol of life and sacrifice in early Christian tradition. In biblical context, aíma symbolizes the divine life force, while elassona conveys a sense of humility and quiet strength. The name Damiella embodies the virtues of compassion, kindness, and inner beauty, reflecting the Christian ideals of selflessness and service.

in_latin.name: Damiella
in_latin.long_meaning: sanguinis nobilitas - nobility of blood; in Latin, the name Damiella signifies a noble and refined individual, strong in character and spirit, reflecting the cultural significance of blood as a symbol of nobility and aristocracy in early Christian tradition. In biblical context, sanguinis conveys the idea of blood as a source of life and vitality, while nobilitas reflects the ideals of dignity, honor, and moral excellence. The name Damiella embodies the virtues of elegance, refinement, and spiritual nobility, reflecting the Christian ideals of purity and holiness.
